Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Stored Assets → WAF Artifacts

WAF artifacts

SATOM's library of file-backed API Protection objects (XML Schema, WSDL, OpenAPI, Lua and others) whose content FortiWeb does not keep in its configuration, so that a policy clone can carry them. WSDL and XSD can be fetched from the application itself.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view protection.edit
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → WAF → WAF Artifacts → Object types / Inventory / Device audit (URL /artifacts/, /artifacts/inventory, /artifacts/audit)

What is it?#

Seven FortiWeb API Protection object types keep only a name in the configuration. Their content is a separate file. A clone that copies configuration alone therefore creates these objects empty, and a rule bound to an empty object fails only after the cutover.

WAF Artifacts is SATOM's own store of those files. It lets a clone or migration upload the real content to the destination. Three of the seven types can't be read back from any FortiWeb one object at a time, so for those SATOM's copy is the only one that can be moved on its own.

The device's Entire configuration backup does carry the content of all three, but inside a block the firmware encrypts, even when you set no backup password, and restoring that backup does not bring them back. Measured on 7.6.8 → 8.0.6, 8.0.6 → 8.0.6 and 7.6.8 → 7.6.8: the restore puts the configuration back and drops every XML Schema and WSDL object, name included. SATOM can't take a single file out of the backup either, so a copy held in SATOM is the only way to move these objects.

Type Can SATOM read it off a device?
XML Schema (XSD) No, upload only
XML DTD Yes
WSDL No, upload only
OpenAPI schema Yes
gRPC IDL No, upload only
JSON Schema Yes
Lua scripting Yes

What does it do?#

The section has three pages, all scoped to the device and ADOM you selected on the Architecture map:

  • Object types (/artifacts/): the catalog of the seven types, how an artifact reaches a server policy, and statistics for this device and ADOM.
  • Inventory (/artifacts/inventory): what SATOM holds for this pair, which server policies need each object, which needed objects are not held, and which held copies are EMPTY. This is where you add content and refresh the index.
  • Device audit (/artifacts/audit): every server policy walked on this device, the artifacts it needs, the Web Protection Profile each one arrives through, and a verdict. It can be exported as JSON (?format=json) or CSV (?format=csv).

Clicking an object opens its page. The page shows the stored versions, the content (and an editor), an A/B diff between any two versions, and the policies that use it.

Verdicts#

Verdict Meaning
ok SATOM holds a copy for this device (or a shared library copy). The policy can move today
borrowed No copy for this device, but another appliance stores the same name. A clone would use those bytes, which is a guess
at-risk No copy anywhere, but the type can still be read from the live FortiWeb. Capture it before the source goes away
blocked No copy anywhere, and no FortiWeb returns this type one object at a time. The policies that need it can't be migrated through SATOM until someone uploads the file

Adding content#

Four ways, all on Inventory. None of them writes to an appliance:

  • Upload a file: the only way a gRPC IDL can enter the store.
  • Fetch from the application: SATOM downloads a WSDL or XML Schema from the service that publishes it, with the schemas it imports from the same host. This is how you bring in the files of a FortiWeb that is already in production.
  • Author content: type or paste the body.
  • Capture from device: SATOM reads the object off this device. This is read-only on the appliance and available for the four readable types only.

Content reaches a device only when the clone/migrate engine creates the object there. There is no separate push button.

A WSDL or XML Schema can import other schemas, and FortiWeb refuses the file if those schemas aren't on the device yet. A clone or migration handles that before its first write: it reads the content it is about to upload and, for every imported schema, moves it ahead in the plan, leaves it alone if the destination already holds it, or adds it from the copy SATOM holds. The pre-flight lists those schemas and which file imports each one; one SATOM can't supply is reported as missing, and the files that import it are skipped.

In Needed by a policy and NOT held, an XML Schema or WSDL row has a Fetch… button. It opens Fetch from the application with the object name filled in and offers, as starting URLs, the real servers behind the policies that use it (read from the device when you open the dialog).

Requirements#

  • A FortiWeb selected as the current device (pick it on the Architecture map). Without one, every page redirects to the map with Pick a device first — <page> is shown for one device and ADOM at a time.
  • For used by information and verdicts: the policy→artifact index for the device. Build it with Refresh the index on the Inventory page, or with the scheduled action artifact_refs.

Permissions#

Action Required
View the three pages, object pages, download or view stored bytes protection.view
Upload, fetch, author/save, capture, delete a version, refresh the index protection.edit or any other permission that grants the legacy config_write (for example protection.apply, network.edit)

Without the permission the page is read-only: Upload a file, Fetch from the application, Author content, Capture from device and the version delete buttons are hidden, the index Refresh button is greyed out, and the object page shows no editor but the reason saving a version needs the config_write permission.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: users without config_write no longer see write buttons that would only fail with 403 Forbidden.

Every write is also checked against the current device. A form aimed at another device is refused with That would have written to a device you are not on. …

How to use#

Find what blocks a migration#

  1. Select the source FortiWeb on the Architecture map.
  2. Open Operations → WAF → WAF Artifacts → Inventory.
  3. In Refresh the index, leave Only this policy (optional) empty, keep Walk budget at 25, and click Refresh. SATOM walks the server policies (read-only) and records which objects each one needs.
  4. Read Needed by a policy and NOT held. Rows marked held elsewhere would be borrowed. The others need content.
  5. Open Device audit and filter Every verdict to blocked for the list of objects nobody can recover. Export it with ?format=csv if needed.

Upload a file#

  1. On Inventory, click Upload a file.
  2. Choose the type and the file. Object name (mkey on the device) defaults to the file name. For OpenAPI the name must end in .json or .yaml. For JSON Schema it must have no extension.
  3. Choose whether the copy belongs to this device and ADOM or is Library-wide (any appliance may use it).
  4. Optionally add a Note (where the file came from), then click Store.

Fetch from the application#

  1. On Inventory, click Fetch from the application.
  2. In URL, enter the address where the service publishes its WSDL or XML Schema, for example https://orders.example.internal/OrderService?wsdl.
  3. In Object name of the first document, enter the name the FortiWeb policy already references (see Needed by a policy and NOT held). Leave it empty to take the name from the URL.
  4. Keep Verify the TLS certificate ticked unless the service uses a self-signed certificate you trust. Optionally add a Note.
  5. Click Fetch and store. The result lists every document stored, the references rewritten, and anything not fetched.

What SATOM does with the document:

  • It follows import, include, redefine and override references on the same host (scheme, host and port), up to 25 documents, 5 levels and 60 seconds. References to another host are listed, not fetched.
  • It stores each document as a new version with the origin fetched and the URL in the note. The first document takes your name; imported schemas are named after their file (OrderService?xsd=1 becomes OrderService-xsd1.xsd).
  • It rewrites each reference it followed to the stored object name. FortiWeb checks a schema's references when the file is uploaded, and opens a relative schemaLocation as an XML Schema object on the device, by name. A reference it did not follow stays as written; FortiWeb then resolves it itself (it downloads an absolute URL during the upload) and refuses the file if it can't.
  • It never follows a redirect, never accepts credentials in the URL, refuses documents that declare a DTD or entities, and never connects to loopback, link-local or SATOM's own addresses.

On the destination FortiWeb, a schema has to exist before the schema or WSDL that imports it.

Capture from the device#

  1. On Inventory, click Capture from device.
  2. Pick one of the four readable types and type the object name exactly as it exists on the device.
  3. Click Capture. SATOM reads the object and stores a version, or reports that it came back empty and stored nothing.

Edit a shared library copy#

  1. Open the object, edit the content and click Save version.
  2. If several device/ADOM pairs read the copy, answer Where does this change go?: All of them (a new version everyone gets), or Only one pair (fork a copy for this device and ADOM only).

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Type One of the seven object types Yes OpenAPI schema
Object name The mkey FortiWeb stores the object under. Empty on upload = the file name Yes orders-api.yaml
Belongs to This device/ADOM, or Library-wide (any appliance may use it) Yes Library-wide
File The content. Max. 4,096 KB. Must not be empty or whitespace-only Upload orders.xsd
URL Fetch: where the service publishes its WSDL or XML Schema. http or https Fetch https://orders.example.internal/OrderService?wsdl
Verify the TLS certificate Fetch: check the service's certificate. On by default No On
Note Provenance recorded on the version No From the API team, v2
Only this policy (optional) Refresh: walk one server policy instead of all No pol-shop-example-com
Walk budget Refresh: maximum policies walked per run (oldest first) No 25

Example#

🧪Example — Migrating an API policy with an XSD

Policy pol-orders on fweb-01 validates XML against the schema xsd-order. Inventory lists xsd-order under Needed by a policy and NOT held, and Device audit shows it as blocked, because XSD can't be read back. The operator gets the original order.xsd from the API team (or fetches the service's ?wsdl with Fetch from the application), stores it as XML Schema (XSD) named xsd-order for this device, and the verdict turns ok. The next clone of pol-orders uploads the schema to the destination when it creates the object.

Result#

  • Uploads, saves and captures store a content-addressed version. Identical content creates no new version, and the flash says so (… — identical to the copy already held or … (unchanged, no new version)).
  • Audit entries: artifact.upload, artifact.fetch (also when nothing was stored, with the reason), artifact.capture, artifact.save, artifact.delete and artifact.refs.
  • A refresh writes only SATOM's own index. It never deletes an edge when a walk fails.

Troubleshooting#

" cannot be read back from any FortiWeb … Upload the file instead."#

Possible causes - You tried to capture XML Schema, WSDL or gRPC IDL.

Solution 1. Use Fetch from the application for a WSDL or XSD the service publishes, or get the original file from whoever authored it and use Upload a file.

Verification - The object appears in Held artifacts, and its verdict is ok.

"Nothing was stored — could not be fetched: refused:
is …"#

Possible causes - The host resolves to loopback, a link-local address or one of SATOM's own addresses. SATOM never fetches from those.

Solution 1. Use the address the service is reachable at on the network, not localhost or the SATOM node.

Verification - The result starts with Fetched from.

"… could not be fetched: redirected to — fetch that URL instead"#

Possible causes - The service answered with a redirect (often to a login page). SATOM doesn't follow redirects.

Solution 1. If the target is the document, fetch that URL. If it's a login page, the WSDL needs authentication: get the file from the service team and upload it.

Verification - The result starts with Fetched from.

"Still pointing at what SATOM did not fetch …"#

Possible causes - A document references a schema on another host, or one that failed to download. It was stored with that reference unchanged.

Solution 1. Fetch or upload the missing schema, and upload or fetch the referencing document again so its reference names the stored object.

Verification - Pushing the document to a FortiWeb no longer fails with device refused the file: … Connecting to '<url>' ….

"device refused the file: Cannot open '/data/etc/xml_schema/root/' to retrieve schema"#

Possible causes - The file references a schema that doesn't exist on the destination FortiWeb under that name, or that hasn't been created yet.

Solution 1. Make sure the referenced schema is stored in SATOM under exactly that name and created on the device first.

Verification - The object is listed on the device under API Protection → XML Protection.

"errcode -3000: Internal error processing requested file. — FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116 refuses every gRPC IDL upload …"#

Possible causes - The destination runs FortiWeb 8.0.6 build0116. It refused every gRPC IDL upload tried (ten contents and archive formats), through SATOM's API path and through the GUI's own session path, while 7.6.8 accepts the same file. The cause is the firmware, not the file.

Solution 1. Open a case with Fortinet for gRPC IDL uploads on 8.0.6 build0116. 2. Until it's fixed, keep gRPC-protected policies on 7.6.8 appliances, or recreate the gRPC rule without the IDL on the 8.0.6 destination.

Verification - The object is listed on the destination under API Protection → gRPC.

" "" came back EMPTY from — nothing was stored."#

Possible causes - The object exists on the device by name, but has no content.

Solution 1. Upload the real file instead.

Verification - The object is listed as held, not as EMPTY.

"The file is empty — there is no content once whitespace is discarded. …"#

Possible causes - The uploaded file has no content apart from whitespace.

Solution 1. Pick the right file and upload again.

Verification - The flash reads Stored <type> "<name>" (<n> bytes).

"Not saved — this copy is read by device/ADOM pairs (…)."#

Possible causes - You edited a shared library copy without saying where the change goes.

Solution 1. Choose All of them or Only one pair under Where does this change go? and save again.

Verification - The flash reads Saved … or Forked … into a copy scoped to ….

"Not saved — no walked policy on this device/ADOM reads this copy, …"#

Possible causes - You chose Only one pair, but no walked policy of the current device reads this copy.

Solution 1. Refresh the index for this device first, or save for all pairs.

Verification - The object page lists this device under Used by.

An object shows "no known user" although a policy uses it#

Possible causes - No walk has recorded the edge yet, or the edge is older than 7 days and shown as stale.

Solution 1. Click Refresh in Refresh the index.

Verification - The object's row lists the policies that use it.

Advanced#

Advanced Storage and scope rules
  • Blobs are stored gzip-compressed and addressed by SHA-256. A version row points at a blob, and deleting a version keeps the blob if another version shares it.
  • Scope is always the session's device. Old links with ?appl= or ?scope= move the session to that device, then reload without the parameter.
  • Stored versions are addressed by id. Blob, raw and delete requests for another device's version answer 404 or are refused.
  • An edge older than 7 days is shown as stale. The scheduled action artifact_refs refreshes the index across the fleet in bounded, oldest-first batches.
  • Content that is not valid UTF-8 is shown with replacement characters, and editing it is refused, so a round trip cannot corrupt the file.
#artifact#xml schema#xsd#wsdl#openapi#grpc idl#json schema#lua#api protection#clone#migration#blocked#fetch#?wsdl#schemaLocation
